newsitem.title: USA: CellStar sees higher Q2 revs from China.
newsitem.headline: CellStar sees higher Q2 revs from China.

text.p: CellStar Corp said Friday its operations in the People's Republic of China have grown notably in 1997, resulting in "significantly increased" revenues in the second quarter, compared to the first quarter, which ended Feb 28.
The company added that these higher revenues are expected to continue as the wireless phone markets there continue to expand.

The growth in China, said CellStar, is due to the expansion of its businesses as a wholesaler of wireless products and as a franchiser of CellStar retail stores. CellStar is the first company, it said, authorized by the Chinese government to sell wireless products there.

As a result of that authorization, in Shenzen, one of the largest cities in China, CellStar is is a joint venture with HonBo, owned by the Shenzen telephone company, to provide service and operate retail wireless product stores. The joint venture, called CellStar-HonBo, operates 10 retail outlets, with CellStar handling the services and HonBo the retail operations.

The company said it has also franchised 12 CellStar stores in 10 large Chinese cities and plans to have about 50 stores by the end of 1997. These franchise stores, which purchase all their inventory from CellStar, sell, activate and provide repair services.
In addition, CellStar said it operates office, warehouse facilities and training centers in Shanghai and Beijing.
The company did disclose revenues for its Asia-Pacific region, but had total revenues of $225.6 million in the seond quarter of 1996, and $256.6 million in the first quarter of this year.
